messages.author: ad331caa97d1c9b0
messages.subject: 'warm' and 'rainoff' in micro_era5
parts:
Hi Mike, 

 

Hope everything goes well!

 

I have several questions about the very cool micro_era5 function.

 

I notice that the micro_era5 function contains two parameters that allow uniformly adjusting hourly temperatures ('warm') and daily precipitation. Can I use them to simulate climate change? Say, for each site, I calculate the predicted changes of temperature and precipitation from WorldClim, and use them for the two parameters in micro_era5? 

 

What I found hard to understand was that the "rainoff" reduced daily rainfall to a negative value if the 'rainoff' was less than zero, and the magnitude of ‘rainoff’ was larger than current rainfall. I also found that the 'rainoff' not only affected rainfall but also temperatures. Even when the daily rainfall was reduced from 0 to a negative value, it would affect temperatures. Given these, does the ‘rainoff’ still produce meaningful simulation of changes in precipitation (and corresponding effects on temperatures)?

 

Your answer will be most appreciated!

 

All the best,

 

Liang

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: 'warm' and 'rainoff' in micro_era5
parts:
Hi Liang,

Yes the 'warm' and 'rainoff' arguments just add offsets to the input air temperature and rainfall vectors. So, if you add a negative value greater than rainfall on a given day, you'll get a negative rainfall. I've now fixed this so rainfall is capped at a lower limit of zero and also made it so you can provide a single offset value or a vector the length of the number of days being simulated, so you can have seasonal changes. All now pushed to github. Let me know if it works.

All the best,
Mike

Hi Mike,

Thanks for revising the codes! Your solution of capping the precipitation by zero makes a lot of sense to me. I have three more questions:

1. What I am doing now is generating the microclimates during a given month before and after climate change. With the latest NicheMapR, I cannot directly calculate my ‘rainoff’ by just dividing the predicted change of total precipitation during a month by the number of days in that month, because in this way, in a drying site, the actual reduction of precipitation would be less than predicted. My plan is: when running the microclimate model for the future climates, I first run the model for current climates and get the current daily rainfall for a given month. I then create a vector of daily rainoff by assigning the predicted change of total precipitation in that month to each day, using the current daily rainfall as weights. Does this way of simulating precipitation change make sense to you?

2. I just updated my NicheMapR. Now following error appears even if I just type in “test<-micro_era5”:

        > test<-micro_era5()
        If program is crashing, try run.gads = 2.

        downloading DEM via package elevatr

        Merging DEMs
        Reprojecting DEM to original projection
        Note: Elevation units are in meters.
        Note: The coordinate reference system is:
        +proj=merc +lon_0=0 +k=1 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs
        extracting weather data locally from c:/era5_data/era5 
        Error in mcera5::point_nc_to_df(nc = paste0(spatial, "_", years, ".nc"),  : 
          unused arguments (long = loc[1], lat = loc[2])
        In addition: There were 17 warnings (use warnings() to see them)

        The warning messages includes:
        16: In showSRID(uprojargs, format = "PROJ", multiline = "NO",  ... :
          Discarded datum World Geodetic System 1984 in CRS definition

          the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used

        I guess this is related to your recent commit on Jan 4th.

3. Another issue I noticed earlier is that, based on the zenith angle, microclimate data generated from micro_era5 seems not starting from 0:00.

Your help would be most appreciated!

All the best,

Liang

Hi Liang,

 

Re 1 – that sounds like the best way to go.

 

Re 2 – try updating micro_era5

 

Re 3 – the dates for the prediction should be in the output item 'dates' – and because it is using UTC it won’t start at local midnight

 

Let me know if that all makes sense.

 

All the best,

Mike
